note: THE decal ART Combat/PlaneDamage.cs's own header deferred: jag/punch/atlasTexture/drawSkinHole/drawSkinTear/drawSkinExit/skinScrapeTexture/drawCraze (planedamage.js:1660-1998), the gap PlaneDamage.cs's note calls out by name ('without this a tear has correct geometry and no surface detail'). Three.js paints these onto an HTML canvas with CanvasTexture; Unity has no canvas, so every shape (jagged closed polygons from the same random-radius-per-angle formula, petal triangles, a sin-modulated lobed opening, branching crack polylines, radial/linear gradients, arc strokes) is evaluated PER PIXEL into a Texture2D instead of rasterized by a 2D context, composited with a standard src-over Over() (canvas's default globalCompositeOperation), with the JS's 'destination-out' punch reproduced as a straight alpha-zero inside the punch polygon. Two documented, narrow simplifications (see the file's own header): strokes use a hard distance threshold instead of canvas's antialiased line rasterizer (invisible at this texture's resolution on an instanced decal metres from the camera), and the handful of radial gradients whose two circles do NOT share a centre (e.g. drawSkinHole's soot) are approximated concentric on the outer circle rather than solving canvas's two-circle conical gradient exactly -- every gradient that IS already concentric in the JS (most of them) is exact. This is the complementary COSMETIC layer around PlaneHull.shader's existing geometric holes (already ported, already has its shader slot) -- not a replacement for it.
verified: Assets/Editor/Probes/CharCombatProbe.cs's DECAL lines report each generated texture's non-transparent pixel fraction (hole/tear/exit/craze atlases, the scrape strip) -- proof the art actually draws ink and is not a blank canvas. NOT run (no editor access). No JS-side pixel ground truth exists to diff against either: tools/_probe_damage.mjs's own canvas shim (its header) no-ops every drawing call (`createRadialGradient`/`fill`/`stroke` etc. all return/do nothing) specifically because Node has no real canvas -- so the JS 'reference' render has never itself been pixel-verified, and this port's per-pixel evaluation is, if anything, the first time this art's actual coverage has been measured at all, on either side.
